html:
Yared was a composer and scholar of Aksum in the 6th century, honoured as a saint. Ethiopian tradition credits him with creating the sacred chant and musical notation of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church.

Aksum had turned Christian in the 4th century, and by Yared's time it was a major trading kingdom on the Red Sea. Tradition says he lived under King Gebre Meskel, who supported his work. His chant, called zema, uses three modes and is still sung by church musicians today. The hymn book Deggua is attributed to him, written in Ge'ez.

Many scholars think the written system of signs for the chant took its full form much later, in the 16th century, and was then credited to him. Even so, Yared stands at the start of one of the oldest living traditions of church music in the world, shared in part with the Eritrean church. His feast day is kept in Ethiopia each year.
sum: Yared was a composer and scholar of Aksum in the 6th century, honoured as a saint. Ethiopian tradition credits him with creating the sacred chant and musical notation of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church.
